s: How were the members of Constituent Assembly elected?
x: Members were indirectly elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies (set up under the 1935 Act), not directly by the public. Princely state representatives were nominated by rulers, but the question concerns elected members.

s: Member of constituent assembly, who drafted the Constitution of India, were-
o: Elected by legislative assemblies of various provinces
Elected by Indian National Congress and Muslim
x: Members of the constituent Assembly were elected by the members of Legislative Assemblies of various provinces. Each province and each Indian State or group of states was allotted the total number of seats proportional to their respective population, roughly in the ratio of one to a million. As a result, 292 members were elected through the Provincial Legislative Assemblies and 4 members represented the Chief Commissioner's Provinces, while the Indian Princely states were allotted a minimum of 93 seats.

s: Which one among the following is an incorrect statement about the Constituent Assembly?
o: It worked with the help of a large number of
It was elected on the basis of universal adult franchise
Its electoral process was based on the sixth schedule
x: The members of the Constituent Assembly were elected by the members of the Legislative Assembly of Provinces on the basis of indirect election, and not on the basis of the Universal Adult franchise. The Members of Provinicial legislatures were themselves elected on the basis of limited franchise, i.e. on the basis of the qualifications of education, property and tax. Universal Adult Franchise enables all citizens to be involved in the governance of their state based on adult suffrage.

Among the following given names, whose portfolio in the first cabinet of India (1947) was different from his portfolio in the Interim Government (1946)? (i) Jagjivan Ram (ii) Dr. Rajendra Prasad (iii) C.H. Bhabha (iv) Sardar Baldev Singh (a) Only (i) and (ii) (b) Only (iii) and (iv) (c) Only (i) and (iii) (d) Only (iii) Chhattisgarh P.C.S. (Pre) 2020 Ans. (d) Portfolios in the Interim Cabinet are as follows: Food and Agriculture - Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Labour- Jagjivan Ram, Defence - Sardar Baldev Singh, Works, Mines and Power - C.H. s: Why did the strength of the Constituent Assembly decline from 389 to 299?

s: From which Act did the restricted franchise used in electing the Constituent Assembly come?
x: The election used the restricted franchise of the 1935 Act, based on tax, education and property qualifications.

s: When were the elections to the Constituent Assembly held?
x: The elections were held in July–August 1946, not June–July; the provincial assembly elections had been held in January 1946.

s: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, what was to be the total strength of the Constituent Assembly?
x: The total strength was 389: 296 from British India and 93 from the princely states.

s: How were the representatives of the princely States in the Constituent Assembly chosen?
o: Elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies
x: Princely representatives were nominated by the rulers; only the provincial members were elected by the Provincial Assemblies.

s: Which of the following describes the nature of the Constituent Assembly of India?
o: Wholly nominated by the British Government
Wholly nominated by the princely rulers
x: The Assembly was partly elected and partly nominated; it was not based on adult franchise.

s: How were the members of the Constituent Assembly from the provinces chosen?
o: Indirectly elected by Provincial Assembly members by proportional representation (single transferable vote)
x: Each community's members in the Provincial Assembly elected their representatives by proportional representation with single transferable vote; there was no adult franchise.

s: How many seats did the Muslim League win in the 1946 Constituent Assembly election?
x: The Congress won 208 seats, the Muslim League 73 and others 15.

s: How many seats were allotted to the Princely States in the Constituent Assembly?
x: Of the 389 planned seats, 296 were for British India and 93 for the Princely States.

s: On which date did representatives of princely states first take their seats in the Constituent Assembly, in its third session?
x: States such as Baroda, Bikaner, Jaipur, Patiala, Rewa and Udaipur joined from the third session on 28 April 1947.

s: From which province was Dr B.R. Ambedkar first elected to the Constituent Assembly?
x: Ambedkar was first elected from East Bengal; later he was elected from the Bombay seat vacated by M.R. Jayakar.

s: Out of the 389 seats planned for the Constituent Assembly, how many were allotted to British India?
x: British India got 296 seats (292 Governor's provinces + 4 Chief Commissioners' provinces); the princely states got 93.

s: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, seats in the Constituent Assembly were allotted in what ratio to population?
x: Seats were allotted roughly one member per 10 lakh (one million) population.

s: Whose vacated seat from Bombay did Dr B.R. Ambedkar fill when he re-entered the Constituent Assembly?
x: Ambedkar was first elected from East Bengal and later from the Bombay seat vacated by M.R. Jayakar.

x: The Constituent Assembly met for the first time on 9 th December 1946. Two hundred and seven representatives, including nine women, were present. Following the French practice of appointing the oldest member as president of the assembly, Dr Sachchidananda Sinha was appointed as the Provisional President of the Assembly. On December 11, 1946, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was appointed as the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly. Later, when India became a republic on January 26 th, 1950, he took the oath as the first President of the Republic of India. Additional Information: Tiruvellore Thattai Krishnamachari (1899 – 1974) was an Indian politician who served as Finance Minister from 1956 to 1958 and from 1964 to 1966. Sources of the Constitution *A major portion of the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Government of India Act 1935 (Blue Print of Indian Constitution). *Rule of law, Parliamentary form of government, Cabinet System, Single Citizenship, Bicameral Legislature, Law making procedures, Parliamentary Privileges and prerogative writs are provisions borrowed from the Constitution of Britain. *Preamble, Judicial review, Independence of Judiciary, Fundamental rights, the post of Vice-President, the procedure of impeachment of President and removal of Supreme Court and High Court judges are provisions taken from the Constitution of the USA. *DPSP (Directive Principle of State Policy), method of election of President and nomination of members to the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) are provisions inspired by the Constitution of Ireland. *Federation with a strong centre, Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, residuary powers to be vested in the centre and appointment of G

Which of the following correctly describes India's status on 15 August 1947?
o: A sovereign republic with no constitutional link to the Crown
A federation of independent princely states
A Dominion with the British monarch as nominal head
A colony governed directly by the British Parliament
x: India became a Dominion on 15 August 1947, with the British monarch as its nominal head.

s: After independence, on whose advice was the Governor-General of each Dominion to act?
x: The Governor-General, common or separate for each Dominion, was to act on the advice of the Dominion ministers.

s: About how many princely states became theoretically free when paramountcy lapsed in 1947?
x: About 565 princely states were theoretically free after paramountcy lapsed, though they were expected to join India or Pakistan.

s: On which date did Kashmir accede to India?
x: Kashmir acceded to India on 26 October 1947 after the tribal invasion.

s: After the Indian Independence Act, 1947, the Constituent Assembly performed which of the following functions?
o: It functioned only as the provincial legislature of the newly formed Union
It functioned as the legislature of British India under the control of the Viceroy
It functioned only as the constitution-making body until 26 January 1950
It functioned both as a sovereign constitution-making body and as the Dominion legislature
x: The Act made the Constituent Assembly fully sovereign in its constitution-making role and also made it the Dominion legislature. The Central Legislative Assembly consequently ceased to function.

s: As what did the Constituent Assembly continue after 26 January 1950?
x: After the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, the Constituent Assembly functioned as the Provisional Parliament until the first general elections held in 1951–52.

s: The immediate historical significance of the Indian Independence Act, 1947 was that it
o: ended provincial autonomy and restored direct British rule over India
combined sovereignty with partition and enabled a quick transfer of power under dominion status
abolished the Constituent Assembly and transferred power to the princely States
created a unitary republic with universal adult franchise
x: The Act gave sovereignty to India in the context of partition. Congress accepted dominion status to facilitate a quick and peaceful transfer of power and to support a strong Centre.

s: Which Act ended British sovereignty over India and gave the Constituent Assembly legislative powers as well?
x: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 ended British sovereignty and gave the Constituent Assemblies both constitution-making and legislative powers.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Last Viceroy of India — C. Rajagopalachari
Last Governor-General of India — C. Rajagopalachari
First Governor-General of independent India — Lord Mountbatten
Last Viceroy of India — Lord Mountbatten
x: C. Rajagopalachari was the last Governor-General, not the last Viceroy. Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy and the first Governor-General of independent India.

s: On which date did the Indian Independence Bill receive royal assent?
x: The Bill was introduced in the Commons on 4 July 1947 and received royal assent on 18 July 1947.

s: On which date was the Indian Independence Bill introduced in the House of Commons?
x: It was introduced on 4 July 1947; royal assent followed on 18 July 1947.

s: On which plan was the Indian Independence Act, 1947 based?
x: The 3 June 1947 Plan of Mountbatten, accepted by the Congress and the League, was the basis of the Act.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Mountbatten Plan:
1. It was announced on 3 June 1947.
2. It was accepted by both the Congress and the Muslim League.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the 3 June 1947 Plan was accepted by the Congress and the League and became the basis of the Act.

s: Who chaired the Punjab and Bengal Boundary Commissions?
x: Radcliffe chaired both Boundary Commissions; the award was published on 17 August 1947.

s: On which date was the Radcliffe award published?
x: The award came out on 17 August 1947, two days after independence.

s: When did Hyderabad sign a Standstill Agreement with India?
x: Hyderabad signed a Standstill Agreement in November 1947; Kashmir acceded on 26 October 1947.

s: On which date did India's dominion status come to an end?
x: Dominion status ended when India became a Republic on 26 January 1950.

s: Who was the last and only Indian Governor-General of India?
x: Rajagopalachari was the last and only Indian Governor-General (June 1948-January 1950); Mountbatten was the first GG of independent India.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Independence Act, 1947:
1. The British Crown lost its veto.
2. The Central Legislative Assembly continued alongside the Constituent Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Crown lost its veto, but the Central Legislative Assembly ended; the Constituent Assembly became the Dominion legislature.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the princely states in 1947?
o: Finance was ceded under the Instrument of Accession.
Defence was ceded under the Instrument of Accession.
Communications were ceded under the Instrument of Accession.
Hyderabad signed a Standstill Agreement in November 1947.
x: The Instrument of Accession ceded defence, external affairs and communications, not finance.

s: Under the Instrument of Accession (1947), a princely state ceded defence, external affairs and which other subject to the Dominion?
x: The Instrument of Accession ceded defence, external affairs and communications, not finance.

s: Which was the first law to receive the assent of C. Rajagopalachari as Governor-General?
x: As Governor-General, C. Rajagopalachari gave assent to the Madras Estates (Abolition) Act on 2 April 1949.

s: On which date did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar warn against the "grammar of anarchy" in his closing speech?
x: Ambedkar used the expression “grammar of anarchy” in his closing speech on 25 November 1949.

s: Critics who called the Indian Constitution a 'patchwork' meant that it was:
o: Drafted without any debate in the Constituent Assembly
Framed by a body elected on adult franchise
Largely borrowed from various other constitutions and sources
Written only by the British Parliament
x: The Constitution was called 'borrowed' or a 'patchwork' because it drew heavily on provisions from various constitutions and sources.

s: About how long did the Constituent Assembly take to complete its work?
x: The Assembly took about three years, for which it was criticised, along with not being based on adult franchise.

s: Who stated that constitutional morality “is not a natural sentiment. It has to be cultivated”?
x: The statement was made by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar on 4 November 1948. The expression was borrowed from George Grote.

s: Since which year has Constitution Day (26 November) been observed?
x: Constitution Day has been observed since 2015, the 125th birth-anniversary year of B.R. Ambedkar.

s: Who called the Constituent Assembly 'a body of Hindus'?
x: Viscount Simon called it 'a body of Hindus'; Granville Austin called it a one-party body in an essentially one-party country.

s: Critics said the Assembly took about 3 years, compared with about how long for the USA?
x: Critics called the Assembly time-consuming: about 3 years against about 4 months for the USA.

s: From whom did Ambedkar borrow his phrase on constitutional morality?
x: Ambedkar's 4 November 1948 remark that constitutional morality has to be cultivated was borrowed from George Grote.

s: Which of the following remarks is correctly matched with its speaker?
o: Delay adult franchise by 15 years – Rajendra Prasad
'A Constitution, like a machine, is a lifeless thing' – Rajendra Prasad
x: Prasad said this on 26 November 1949; 'Drifting Committee' was Naziruddin Ahmed's, 'a body of Hindus' Viscount Simon's, and Maulana Azad wanted adult franchise delayed.

s: The Constituent Assembly is said to have taken 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to frame the Constitution. This period is counted between which two dates?
x: From the first meeting on 9 December 1946 to adoption on 26 November 1949 is 2 years, 11 months and 18 days.

s: Who called the Drafting Committee a 'Drifting Committee'?
x: Naziruddin Ahmed mocked the Drafting Committee as the 'Drifting Committee'.

s: Who said that the Constituent Assembly represented 'only one major community' in India?
x: Winston Churchill said the Assembly represented only one major community; Viscount Simon called it 'a body of Hindus'.

s: For how many days did the Drafting Committee, chaired by Dr B.R. Ambedkar, sit?
x: The seven-member Drafting Committee chaired by Ambedkar sat for 141 days.
